To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ensembles of hierarchical multi label decision tress are competitive with state-of-the-art statistical methods for ORF function prediction, and that the trees in the ensemble are more interpretable than the models of the statistical methods.

1) Decision tree based methods are an easy to use and efficient alternative to more complicated statistical learning and functional link methods for predicting gene functions.2) Ensembles of decision trees can be used to predict multiple gene functions simultaneously, while respecting a predefined hierarchy of functions.3) The ensemble method is competitive with state of art methods for ORF function prediction, while being easy to use.
1) hierarchical multi-label decision trees can be learned efficiently and 2) ensembles of such decision trees can be used for accurate prediction of gene function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for the prediction of gene functions.
the problem of automatically assigning biological functions to the open reading frames (ORFs) in the genome of an organism.
the development of a novel algorithm and the evaluation of a new method for predicting the function of genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
decision tree ensembles are a competitive approach to ORF prediction, with a good predictive performance and an easy to use and efficient implementation.
decision tree based models, in particular hierarchical ensembles of multi label decision trees, are a state of art, efficient, easy to use and competitive approach to ORF prediction.
hierarchical multi label decision-tree ensembles are a state of-the-art, efficient and easy-to-use method for predicting ORF functions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the hierarchical multi label decision-tree ensembles are competitive with the state of the art methods in terms of predictive accuracy and are more efficient and easier to use than the state of the arts methods.

we present a new hierarchical multi label decision algorithm, which outperforms the previously described methods for learning hierarchical multi-label decision trees, and we show that decision tree based ensemble methods for function prediction are competitive with state-of-the-art methods.
the hierarchical multi label decision ensemble approach is a good compromise between predictive power, efficiency and usability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ensemble methods are to be preferred over single decision trees.
ensemble methods are more accurate than individual decision trees, but that they are still less accurate than the best statistical learning methods.
ensembles of decision trees, which are computationally efficient, can be competitive with state of art methods for ORF function prediction.
